sections.heading: C — Speed and Speed Limits
sections.markdown:
## C — Speed and Speed Limits

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Drivers match the traffic stream while honoring every limit, keeping two seconds behind leaders at thirty miles per hour or less, four seconds above thirty, more in poor conditions, four seconds always for beginners, and any fixed-object gap under two seconds marks tailgating [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Average drivers need one and a half seconds to think, react, and brake, and total stopping stretches climb from sixty-three feet at twenty miles per hour to three hundred eighty-seven feet at seventy with good brakes and tires on dry level pavement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Speed and gaps flex with driver fitness, vehicle state, and road state, tired or ill drivers stay parked, wet, crowded, and blind conditions earn slower wider driving with full control, and nobody outdrives visible road in dark or weather [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Vision spans one hundred eighty degrees or more standing still, then shrinks to about two-thirds at twenty miles per hour, two-fifths at forty, and one-fifth at sixty [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A02
Posted minimums and maximums bind under normal flow, heavy traffic, weather, and gloom demand slower wider driving, and cities and counties may reset limits but must hold day and night equal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
Maximums run thirty miles per hour in urban districts, fifteen in alleys, and fifteen on beaches and beach-adjacent county roads where declared [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
Outside urban districts numbered highways allow seventy miles per hour generally or sixty for inspected school buses, unnumbered roads allow sixty generally or fifty for uninspected or off-system school buses, studies may raise or lower limits, many limited-access highways post seventy-five to eighty-five, and posted signs always rule [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Past lit stopped medical, law, fire, tow, utility, and road-work vehicles drivers drop twenty below the limit or abandon the nearest lane on multi-lane roads [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
Mail, delivery, and trash trucks stopping often earn cautious passing with lane changes where possible [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
Street racing bans races, speed contests, drag and acceleration contests, driver endurance tests, and drag-linked speed exhibitions or records, punishing convictions from Class B misdemeanor to second-degree felony for the deadly crashes and road damage they bring [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0052]

items.why: Section Eight is rule-and-threshold recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Texas Driver Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so Section Eight speed rules change at most with new editions.
